The sharp distinctions: (a) the 4.8-6 kW figure IS in P1 but is NOT printed, because printing a rating is a claim about what the LABEL says, and nothing describes THIS unit's label — a fact being TRUE of the device does not make it PRINTED on it; (b) the catalogue number PXTC1ARA IS printed, unlike the Axis (model unknowable from an OUI), because P1 names the variant explicitly and a part number a rack chassis actually carries is what the evidence supports. The discipline is 'print what the evidence supports', not 'print less'.

mechanical.notes: 9/9 suites. Console clean. THE DEFECT: the livery plate was printed OVER a removable module — it fell on the 3rd PSU bay (30x4 mm overlap with its cavity, face and handle). A manufacturer wordmark silkscreened on a hot-swap component is not a livery. Why nothing saw it: the plate was in-envelope, attached, right size, right colour — every existing guard was satisfied; being in the WRONG PLACE is not a property any of them measured. Moved to the free band between the bays (16.5 mm) and the chassis top (21.5 mm) — the 5 mm a 1U front actually leaves for print, of which the plate takes 3.5 with margin. New guard verifyLiveryIsOnTheChassis (a printed mark may not overlap any piece that is not the chassis body); negative control: returning the plate reports 3 overlaps, as-built 0. Right-sized by measurement (canvas 1024x82 = 1.79x worst case; 512 would interpolate letters up) AND aspect-asserted (plate 12.57:1 vs canvas 12.49:1, 0.7% distortion, so letters can't stretch unnoticed). Verified: ratings null, no rating-shaped string, no bay numbering/series/QR; artwork rasterises once, no http/fetch/Image; 6 materials over 6 groups (2 unique) with art only on group 4 (+z, the rack-chassis front); wrap-around guard fires 1 on a single mapped material over 6 groups, 0 as-is; traceability walks material ARRAYS and matches clones by id prefix with no coded exception; exposure/contrast/framing/float all unchanged.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. Two things make this pass strong. First, a genuinely subtle defect: the livery sat on a removable module and every existing guard passed it, because 'wrong place' was a property none of them measured — caught, moved to the real 5 mm print strip, and closed with a new guard + negative control. Second, the text-discipline distinctions are the sharpest of the run: a TRUE rating (4.8-6 kW, which IS in P1) is still not printed because printing is a claim about the LABEL, not the product; but the catalogue number PXTC1ARA IS printed because the evidence names the variant — 'print what the evidence supports', neither fabricating (the Axis model) nor omitting (the evidenced part number). I verified the livery text and the absence of ratings/bay-numbers directly in a crop. Cleared to the lighting-camera pass.
